title: Two True, One Invented · Pair relay
hook: Find a game, gather your friends and start playing.

knows: The group wants an activity to play together.
doesNotKnow: The setup, turn and ending for this house-rule format.

misconception: The group has to know a complicated rulebook before starting.
objective: Learn how to play Two True, One Invented · Pair relay with friends.

claims.text: Original house rules: The lead chooses three comfortable-to-share statements about themselves: two true and one invented. The lead says all three statements and the others choose which one is invented. The group identifies the invented statement; anyone may skip a turn. Form pairs. On each pair’s turn, both people make separate attempts with fresh challenges, helping only their partner. The pair earns one point only if both succeed. Each pair has two turns. Highest score wins.
claims.source: Original playable house-rule proposal; not an authoritative ruleset for a traditional game.

claims.text: For this version: 4, 6 or 8 players; materials: Paper and pencil.
claims.source: Proposed setup and player range for this activity.

recall.question: In Two True, One Invented, what counts as a successful turn?
options: The lead skips the turn without attempting it.
The group ends the round before anyone plays.
The group identifies the invented statement; anyone may skip a turn.
recall.why: The group identifies the invented statement; anyone may skip a turn.
